name: tiko-lang
description: Language support for the tiko programming language: diagnostics, completion, hover, go to definition, references, rename, formatting and more. The language server is included. Tiko is a FreeBASIC-compatible language.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Starting tiko-lsp runs an executable named in settings or found in the workspace.

tiko.server.path.markdownDescription: Path to a `tiko-lsp` executable to use instead of the one included with the extension. Empty: the included server, then `tiko-lsp` on the `PATH`, then `bin/tiko-lsp(.exe)` inside a workspace folder.

tiko.server.arguments.markdownDescription: Arguments passed to the server. Add `--log-level`, `debug`, `--log-file`, `C:/temp/tiko-lsp.log` to see what it is doing; it never writes to stdout.

tiko.toolchainPath.markdownDescription: The folder you unpacked tiko into -- the one named `tiko-lang`, e.g. `C:/tiko-lang` (Linux/macOS: `/home/you/tiko-lang`). Its headers, packages and compiler are then used, so `std/` and `windows.bi` names complete. Empty: a `tiko` on the `PATH`, then a `tiko-lang` folder in your home or Downloads folder, is found automatically. **Tiko: Locate Toolchain...** sets this for you. Sent as `initializationOptions.toolchainPath`.

tiko.includePaths.markdownDescription: Usually unnecessary: `tiko.toolchainPath` sets this. Directories `#include "windows.bi"` is found in -- the toolchain's `inc`, e.g. `C:/tiko-lang/inc` (Linux/macOS: `/home/you/tiko-lang/inc`). The server reads the headers the workspace includes from here, so Win32, AfxNova and runtime names complete, hover and show signatures. Sent as `initializationOptions.includePaths`.

tiko.packagePaths.markdownDescription: Where `#import "std/strings"` is found -- the toolchain's `pkg`. Usually unnecessary: the `pkg` beside an include path is found on its own. Sent as `initializationOptions.packagePaths`.

tiko.compilerPath.markdownDescription: A `tiko` the server may ASK about each workspace folder's `tiko.toml` (`tiko metadata`): imports then resolve where the compiler resolves them, `-i` options included, and the `tiko/metadata` request returns the package's targets. Never run for diagnostics. Empty: the compiler in `tiko.toolchainPath`, else a `tiko` on the `PATH`. Sent as `initializationOptions.compilerPath`.

tiko.build.arguments.markdownDescription: Extra compiler options for **Tiko: Build** and **Tiko: Run**, such as `-g` (debug information) or `-exx` (runtime checks). A project's `tiko.toml` profiles still apply.

tiko.run.arguments.markdownDescription: Command-line arguments passed to the program by **Tiko: Run** (after `--`).

tiko.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and tiko-lsp in the 'Tiko Language Server' output channel.

file.description: A root file to build instead of the project: absolute, or relative to the workspace folder. Empty: the tiko.toml at or above the active file, else the active file.

target.description: The tiko.toml target to run, when it has more than one exe target. Empty: the one holding the active file, else the one chosen with Tiko: Select Run Target...

args.description: Compiler options, such as -g or -exx. Default: tiko.build.arguments.

runArgs.description: Arguments for the program. Default: tiko.run.arguments.
